touches.text: Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
A diagnostic report, EXACTLY like the Trouble Tickets in the Number Five Crossbar Telephone Switch. It MUST include EVERYTHING needed to diagnose, isolate, and repair the trouble.
The test before raising one: can only CC or Akien fix this? If not, it is a log line, not a trouble. One problem, one trouble.
They show on the operator's to-do list (7.3.6).

A trouble ticket is a work order. Whoever fixed it reports the fix to the originator (the device or machine that raised it), and the originator marks it fixed. A trouble that comes back is not designed for yet; if recurrent problems appear, we'll explore that.

Its web panel is the operator's to-do list: email, trouble tickets, open questions (the ones only the operator can answer). The list is live: items appear as they arrive and leave as they're answered or resolved.
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.
A second observation of an open trouble NEVER issues a new ticket; it increments a counter on the open one.

A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.
conflicts.ticket_says: When a door refuses to write a red's ticket, the ticket stays new and is retried on the next run; no ticket is written in the refused run. Instead, an unticketed trouble is raised naming the door and its lacks.
conflicts.why: The outline states 'Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds...unless one is already open for it.' There is no stated exception for when a ticketing door refuses. The ticket's implementation skips the write when the door refuses, which violates the outline's prescriptive requirement. The ticket addresses this via constraints (keeping the red new and retryable, raising a trouble for human intervention) but the core statement 'each run writes a ticket' becomes false when the door refuses.
